names.name: Cutting by hand
names.said: A shop that says hand-cut on the window is drawing a line, and everyone in the trade knows which one.

text.what: Rolling sheeted dough and cutting rings with a two-ring cutter, rather than depositing or buying pre-formed shells.
text.story: Cutters with two concentric circles were on sale by 1870, which is when the ring and its hole became a manufactured thing rather than a trick with a pepper box. A ring can also be made by joining the ends of a rope of dough, or by stretching a disc until the middle tears.
text.how: Sheet, cut in rows, lift the rings onto screens, gather and re-roll the scrap once — twice makes it tough.
text.today: Hand-cut is a claim a shop makes on its sign. This project records the claim and its source, and does not test it.
